title: Cyclotomic class groups, Stickelberger and Herbrand–Ribet
summary: A target-level plan of finite cyclotomic class groups and their tame characters, cyclic units and capitulation, integral Stickelberger annihilation at every conductor, Herbrand–Ribet, Kummer regularity and units, all prime-power unit indices, cyclotomic growth and Mazur’s inverse-character obstruction. Every prime is included, with dyadic and exceptional-character boundaries explicit. Supplier requests and three precise gaps remain; no formalization claim is made.
readme: General cyclotomic arithmetic for every prime and every prime-power level, with full Stickelberger annihilation for all conductors. The finite core follows ClassFieldTheory. Native ideal classes, full unit groups and arithmetic Frobenius fix the conventions; odd-prime integral tame projections never become sign projections at 2. Herbrand–Ribet is proved by the modular converse. The tower layer specializes the existing general Iwasawa theory; the finite-unit ownership moves and two-roadmap packaging proposal are explicit. Vandiver remains a conjecture. See the companion reader for the complete statements, APIs, tests and source locators.

stages.title: Finite cyclotomic class groups and tame characters
stages.description: For every prime p and r≥1 use K_(p,r)=Q(ζ_(p^r)), its native ideal class group and p-primary module A_(p,r). Compare Artin conjugation with the covariant ideal action. For odd p specialize integral tame Teichmüller projectors at every level, retain the wild action and prove real transfer. At p=2 preserve the integral sign defects. Identify the unique prime over p as principal and its unramified splitting quotient with A_(p,r).

stages.title: Hilbert 90–94, relative units and capitulation
stages.description: Specialize the existing field Hilbert 90 without claiming a unit-valued lift. For arbitrary cyclic prime-degree number-field extensions with no infinite ramification, construct the saturated relative unit lattice and prove Hilbert 91’s independence modulo 1−σ and Hilbert 92’s cohomology count. Prove Hilbert 93’s different/invariant-ideal assertions, construct the capitulation cocycle and prove Hilbert 94’s exact kernel count in the everywhere-unramified case. Supply one-prime p-class control for all finite Galois p-extensions.

stages.title: The integral Stickelberger ideal and annihilation
stages.description: For every conductor m≥2 define the rational element θ_m with inverse group-ring basis, the denominator ideal J_m, the integral Stickelberger image I_m and positive floor-coefficient smoothings. Prove Gauss-sum descent and ideal factorization with explicit residue-character compatibility. Deduce integral annihilation of the full class group, including even and composite conductors.

stages.title: Bernoulli values, reflection and Herbrand’s theorem
stages.description: Compare character evaluation of θ_p with the existing generalized Bernoulli numbers and ordinary B_k/k modulo p. Treat the exceptional ω component by integral smoothing. Prove Herbrand’s implication and reflection, with the different constant-dual and Kummer-dual character shifts distinguished. Compare native analytic class-number and regulator formulas with primitive-character products for CM abelian fields.

stages.title: Ribet’s modular converse
stages.description: For every irregular pair (p,k), 2≤k≤p−3 even, prove the relative class-number bound needed for the weight-two auxiliary form and the integral Eisenstein congruence. Specialize the supplied newform realization and oriented nonsplit lattice theorem. Prove small-ramification finite-flat local splitting, form the residual splitting field compositum with Q(ζ_p), and obtain Ribet’s everywhere-unramified elementary abelian extension. Deduce the full Herbrand–Ribet equivalence independently of a main conjecture.

stages.title: Regular primes and Kummer’s lemma at every level
stages.description: Define regularity for every prime by total cyclotomic class-number indivisibility and prove Kummer’s Bernoulli criterion for odd primes. Prove the primary-unit radical criterion and Kummer’s integer-congruent unit lemma. Propagate vanishing to every odd regular prime-power level, and prove odd class number at every dyadic level, handling Q and Q(i) before cyclic unit arguments.

stages.title: Cyclotomic units, class-number indices and Vandiver
stages.description: For every prime-power conductor define circular numbers inside the field and intersect with integral units, retaining sign torsion at conductor two. Prove the ratio generators, real root corrections, Hasse index and full-to-real unit quotient. Establish the cyclotomic unit index h(K^+) at every level, including the dyadic adaptation. Define the per-prime Vandiver predicate, identify its equivalent even-component and unit-quotient vanishing conditions, and state universal Vandiver only as a conjecture.

stages.title: Cyclotomic towers and class-number growth
stages.description: Specialize the existing inverse-norm class module and general Iwasawa growth theorem to the cyclotomic towers F_n=Q(ζ_(p^(n+1))) for odd p and F_n=Q(ζ_(2^(n+2))) for p=2. Prove equivariant Artin comparison and exact coinvariant control using the unique totally ramified prime. Deduce the eventual μp^n+λn+ν valuation formula for all primes and zero valuations at all regular and dyadic levels. Generic inverse limits, compact Iwasawa modules and the theorem for arbitrary Z_p-extensions keep their existing owner.

stages.title: Mazur’s inverse-character obstruction
stages.description: Prove Mazur’s inverse low odd-character vanishing at conductor p and propagate it to every prime-power level by exact control and compact Nakayama, with the p=691 exception for exponent −11. Show every everywhere-unramified abelian p-quotient of character ω⁻¹ is trivial and that killing the principal conductor prime does not change the Hilbert p-class quotient. Compare constant-coefficient étale H¹ with the inverse-character dual and μ_p coefficients with the twisted dual. Export the precise conditional division-field obstruction to the Eisenstein-ideal roadmap.
